prompt_text: overhead editorial photograph of a physical scorecard rig on a steel workbench, with several weighted evaluation lanes built from tokens, clips, and evidence sockets feeding into one final comparison tray; the structure should show dimension groups and relative weight through object size, spacing, and material emphasis rather than donut charts, stacked bars, or labels. no readable text, no labels, no numbers, no dashboard UI, no chart board look, no generic slide layout, no decorative software schematic. Target aspect ratio: 16:9 Critical render rule: do not generate any readable text, letters, numbers, captions, labels, logos, watermarks, slide titles, document copy, dashboard copy, UI text, headline text, wall text, or typographic overlays anywhere in the image. If a screen, board, document, dashboard, scorecard, or interface is visible, it must contain only abstract non-readable blocks, simple shapes, and soft placeholder marks. Never place large title words, marketing slogans, section headers, or composited text for later overlay; leave that area visually quiet and empty instead. Use unlabeled structure, simple shapes, tokens, lanes, connectors, and status cues instead of screenshot-like dashboards or reports. Analytical image rule: avoid screenshot aesthetics, whiteboard snapshots, slide decks, tables with headers, and infographic panels with text. Prefer a premium enterprise visual metaphor built from cards, modules, flows, physical markers, subtle charts without labels, and clean operational structure. Do not label stages directly inside the image; represent system stages through position, grouping, material contrast, and abstract markers only.
negative_prompt: five-star rating cliches, donut chart, stacked bar chart, software score screen, readable weight labels.
alt_text_en: visualize a repeatable buying scorecard as a small set of weighted evaluation dimensions anchored in evidence.
